question: Which cross-type settings copies does Factorio allow, and what do they write? In particular, what request counts does an assembling machine put on a logistic chest?
answer: All three cross-type pairs the TODO names are allowed and do real work: assembling machine -> logistic chest (requests), assembling machine -> inserter (filters), and train stop <-> locomotive (colour, both directions). An assembling machine onto a plain container does nothing.

theFormulaInTheIssueIsWrong.reading: Thirty seconds of production of each ingredient, floored. The two rules disagree on every case probed: for assembling-machine-2 on electronic-circuit the recorded rule gives 1 iron plate where the game asks for 30.
theFormulaInTheIssueIsWrong.flooring: assembling-machine-2 on processing-unit gives 4.5 advanced circuits and asks for 4; assembling-machine-3 gives 7.5 and asks for 7. Floor, not round.
theFormulaInTheIssueIsWrong.modules: The machine's actual speed counts, not its prototype's. assembling-machine-2 with two speed modules (0.75 * 1.4) asked for 62 iron plates where the arithmetic says 63 - float error in the game's own multiplication, which JavaScript reproduces when the terms are multiplied in the same order.
theFormulaInTheIssueIsWrong.fluids: Fluid ingredients are left out entirely rather than requested at zero - processing-unit's sulfuric acid does not appear.

provenance.caveat: The only Factorio on this machine is 2.1.12; this editor targets 2.0.45-2.0.73. Behaviour is assumed stable across that range but was not measured on a 2.0.x binary.

cases.note: electronic-circuit declares no energy_required; 0.5 is the prototype default, which these numbers confirm
sulfuric-acid x5 is a fluid and is absent from the result
One short of the exact figure, in the game's own float arithmetic. This is the case that proves modules are counted at all.
A buffer chest takes the requests the same way a requester chest does

cases.wrote: nothing - and the chest's existing requests were CLEARED, leaving an empty section

cases.note: Ingredient names only. An inserter filter carries no count, so none of the thirty-seconds arithmetic appears here.

cases.role: control - a cross-type pair that should do nothing
cases.wrote: nothing. A plain container has no requests to write, and the game leaves it alone, which is why `container` is not in the editor's CROSS_TYPE_PASTE map.

cases.note: The name is not carried. The game also clears copy_color_from_train_stop, which the editor does not model.
The stop kept its own station name, so colour really is the whole of this pair in both directions

cases.role: control - a same-type pair known to copy

notImplemented: import_from: "nauvis" rides along on every request the game writes. It is a Space Age interplanetary-import field the editor does not model, and it is deliberately not written - a blueprint that arrives carrying one keeps it, since the filter setter preserves fields it does not know.
copy_color_from_train_stop, set to false on a locomotive that receives a stop's colour. Not modelled by IEntity.
